data.narrative:
Peak Energy, a Series A climate and energy company founded by Landon Mossburg and Liam O'Connor, has raised $65M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of 8 private peers and 1 public comparable (Linazo, LNZA), though narrower same-stage and adjacent-stage peer sets proved insufficient for robust median-based triangulation.

The Stage-Progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the $65M total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of $130M. This method is appropriate given Peak Energy's clear stage classification and capital structure, though it relies on standardized stage advancement rather than company-specific operating metrics. The Peer-Median approach was not applicable; while 8 same-sector peers exist (including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, and KoBold Metals), none of the narrow filters—same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier—yielded three or more datapoints necessary for statistical reliability. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable methodology risk.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $110M to $150M, with a median of $130M. This range reflects the quantifiable upside and downside from a single applicable method, absent triangulation from peer multiples. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable-stage climate tech transactions and reliance on stage-based rather than revenue or unit-economics-based scaling. Further analysis would benefit from access to recent Series A exit data or operating metrics within the climate tech vertical.
